Job Title: Computer vision / machine learning: synthetic video to real video
Description:
Our company is working on a government proposal involving synthetic video data, which will be used to train object detection and tracking networks. The synthetic data will be high-fidelity video using ray tracing, but there is an opportunity to make it more realistic using Domain Adaptation (DA).

The synthetic data will be in video form, so it's important to use video-to-video translation approaches that provide temporal consistency. 

There are two components of this effort:

1. Come up with a compelling approach and write it up in a proposal.
2. Be included as a performer on the proposal, as a subject matter expert (SME).

The ideal candidate would perform both components. We want to strengthen our proposal by including an SME, so this person would likely need to have publications in this area. Our team has significant expertise in computer vision and machine learning in general, but limited experience in video-to-video translation.

I am looking for assistance with a trade analysis project. 

The project is to acquire data from UN COMTRADE and then process it via comparison between different tariff regimes for trading partners for a group of countries.

The group and tariff rates to use would be identified to successful candidate. 

It is estimated at 8 days work.

STEP ONE
Using COMTRADE acquire data on global imports for a GROUP OF COUNTRIES as a group by value at 6 digit tariff code for sample year 2019.

STEP TWO 
Filter to top 100 imports by value (equating to minimum imports per line of approx. value of over 135,000 USD per annum for whole of GROUP OF COUNTRIES)

STEP THREE
Acquire the Applied MFN tariff being used in each of the  countries within the GROUP for these top 100 tariffs and illustrate alongside the country specific tariff (to be provided) applied in 2023 and 2027.

STEP FOUR
Itemise for these 100 import lines the current MFN Applied rate, the Country specific duty rate for 2023 and the Country specific duty rate for 2027. 

STEP FIVE
Exclude all lines which are duty free under MFN Applied rate or which are excluded from country specific liberalisation.   If less than 50 tariff lines remain, steps 1-5 above to be repeated until we have a minimum of 50 tariff lines to analyse. 

STEP SIX
Acquire  country specific import data on those 100 import lines for each the 15 countries in the GROUP by volume and value; specifying top 3 MFN current exporters.

STEP SEVEN
Calculate unit cost per kg or litre for each tariff line

STEP EIGHT
Calculate Duty payable by unit under country specific agreement in 2023 and in 2027; and under Applied MFN per unit; and the total cost by volume/weight quoted for country specific agreement 2023, 2027 and MFN. 

STEP NINE
Calculate the Value of the switch in tariff for the GROUP buyer country from MFN to country specific tariff for 2023 and 2027 (total and by unit) 

STEP TEN
Produce abbreviated sheet illustrating the US dollar saving by unit and by total volume and giving a ranking of greatest saving by product line for each of 15 GROUP countries for 2023 and 2027.

About the game:

A card is drawn randomly from a well shuffled deck of cards. The drawn card is placed back into the deck, which is then reshuffled, before the following card is drawn..

Cards are divided into three categories- A,B & C. Category A has 6 cards (Ace-6), Category B has 4 cards (7-10) and category C has 3 cards (J,Q,K). The objective is to predict which card category will open next.
These prediction can be done in 2 ways
1.  model predicts which category will open next.
2.  the model predicts which category will not open next.
Both the methodologies will have different payout and penality.

1. If prediction is A and it's correct then reward is 1 X bet amount else penality is 1 X bet amount

3. If prediction is C and it's correct then reward is 3 X bet amount else penality is 1 X bet amount

Method 2:
1. If prediction is not A and it's correct then reward is 1 X bet amount else penality is 1.5 X bet amount
2. If prediction is not B and it's correct then reward is 1 X bet amount else penality is 2.5 X bet amount
3. If prediction is not C and it's correct then reward is 1 X bet amount else penality is 3.5 X bet amount

Average Stats is that Out of 100 drawn, there are nearly 25Cs, 35Bs and 45As. Can we build something that correctly predicts these categories once with high confidence.

Job Title: Data collection and labeling - warehouse images & videos
Description:
We are building Computer Vision and Deep Learning algorithms for safety systems in the warehouse. To train and evaluate the performance of the developed systems, we need labeled data (images and videos).

The collected data should be a representative subset of warehouse environments, which should cover as wide variations of warehouse appearance as possible. 

While it is challenging to define the boundaries of variations to be covered, the general rule is – the less similarity between captured images the better. A bad example of a data collection environment is to collect all, e.g. 1000, images from a single passage of a warehouse with minimal changes in the field of view. A good example, collect 1000 images from multiple warehouses with significant changes in the scenery and lighting conditions. Variations in training data are making the system more robust towards unseen data, which is a fundamental property for real-world operating conditions.

Quality
Prior to the data labeling stage, it is important to check the quality of the collected images, keeping the ones satisfying quality criteria. In the initial stage, quality control can be done by a human annotator. Common issues to avoid are bright/saturated or too dark images, blurry images, and low-resolution images (when scraping from the web). As a general criterion, objects of interest, e.g. pallets, and floor, should be easily identifiable by the human annotator.

Data labeling/annotation.
The data to be used for system development is composed of two components:
1. images of warehouse environments, discussed in the section above,
2. labels/annotations done by human experts defining regions of interest in the images, discussed in this section.

For the purposes of labeling/annotation, we will provide our custom annotation tool, allowing you to manually draw the masks for the objects of interest. More details and training will be provided to the selected candidate.

Job Title: Need a Full Stack Developer for Creating A Web App using Various APIs
Description:
I want to create a web app either in Java or Python that will communicate with 4 APIs and record responses in a step-by-step manner to create content through OpenAI GPT technology.

The whole Process would be like this:

1.) App will communicate with the SpaceSerp API for a query and record the results and remove those results on the fly having negative list domains. (https://spaceserp.com/)

2.) After this, app will communicate with Frase NLP API with the same query and results received from SpaceSerp API and would receive json data containing each page's HTML data.

It will convert that json data into nicely organized view so user can select the relevant part from each page to own editor. I will show this to you over virtual call.

Apart from this, the json response also contains common words used in all pages, so app will record them also and show them on the right panel. 

3.) Once user has selected relevant sections from each page content to own editor. He will hit the command to operate next Step.

4.) Once, user has hit the command to operate next step, app will take the whole content from the User's editor and divide them into original sections and run sequential commands and generate the content through Frase Content Creation API. The Input would be Copied Section + Custom Prompt.

5.) Once concatenated all the generated content, it will run the operation of One sentence per paragraph. Then it will show side by side, Input content and concatenated generated Content. Generated Content would be editable by the User. Once he is satisfied, he can submit it to Wordpress through Rest API. The Editor would show content as Title, meta Description, Content. This final step would mark that query/keyword as completed.

To accomplish all of this, there would be one Admin Area and One Employee Area.

Admin Area will firstly Create Employees and generate their Usernames & passwords.

Then Admin will define negative list of domains as required in first communication with the SpaceSerp API.

Then Admin will create a Project and assign that to one or more Employees created in first Step. Apart from this, project details would include a text Area where I will input keywords (One per line) and define Rest API details connection with the Wordpress for that particular project.

Then In Admin Area, I will create prompts and their order of execution that are basically commands which will be used for content generation in Employee Area as stated above. It will be name of the prompt & prompt text.

Admin Area will also contain fields for Adding SpaceSerp API & Frase API.

In the Employee Area, he will see the queries which haven't been marked completed in the last step as defined above. He will Click on any pending query in his dashboard home screen and app will execute first command by communicating SpaceSerp and show him the results. He can manually add or delete any URL at this stage and click "Process". This will trigger the Second communication with Frase NLP API and receive json response and process that json file and show it in an organized way while keeping HTML tags like if it 's heading h2, h3 or h4 and it's supporting content labeled in p tag, li, ul tags, so basically everything until wither next h tag or end of document.

The user will first define the Title of Content, then define meta Description manually. Then he will choose best sections from all the received pages along with their heading and supporting content and it will be keep adding in his own editor. Once he is satisfied with his outline and content, he will press the button "Write". Then it will trigger communication with Frase API in loop, section by section and adding the content to different editor.

Once user is satisfied with the desired content, he will press submit, and it will trigger the Rest API connection with the Wordpress based on the project he is working on.

I am attaching the json file received from Frase NLP API for your reference. To convert it to excel table, you can use https://www.aconvert.com/document/json-to-xls/

Job Title: Python developer to create web scraping scripts for an ongoing role
Description:
You will create scrapers using Python in multiple milestones.

Guidelines
* Python2/3 is acceptable. Please minimize use of dependencies that I can't just pip install.
* Avoid using frameworks and keep to as flat file procedural code as possible.
* As a general rule scrape all data available unless otherwise instructed.
* By default dump to raw data format provided by data source, acceptable syntax are (1)JSON (2)XML (3)HTML (4)PDF
* Reduce parsing so collection doesn't break on source fields / structure changes.  When parsing, do it as a secondary output format.

Arguments:
(M) [scrapeid] scraper module to call, each representing a website data source
(O) [-f | --file] if specified, write output to filename. If folder is not provided save to default output folder (configuration). If unspecified – output to STDOUT
(O) [-s | --syntax] syntax to use. this is helpful in case scraper can output more than one format. each scraper module has a default syntax used if unspecified
(O) [-c | --compress] boolean, accepts true/false. default = true. if saving to file - compress in memory and add a .gz suffix (don't use any temporary files). If sending to STDOUT - disable compression.
-- (M)andatory | (O)ptional

Examples:
$ python crawl.py src1 -f output.json
## load src1 scraper, result scrape is saved as output.json.gz in default output directory
$ python crawl.py -f /tmp/data.json --compress false
## load src2 scraper - result scrape is saved as /tmp/data.json
$ python crawl.py --syntax html
## load src1 scraper - result scrape is sent to STDOUT in html format

Note - I have a need to scrape many data sources | parse unstructured data to serialize it into JSON | do ongoing maintenance and troubleshooting. The applicant that will deliver this with high quality code and a professional attitude can become an ongoing role.

Job Title: Developing a Deep Learning model for eye gaze prediction as part of a research study

The success criteria we apply is achieving a predefined loss value for the test set. This test set will be available to the participants. However, the loss function will not be provided, as the participants are expected to implement their own task-specific loss function. To guide the improvement of the DL model, we will provide the participants with the loss value for each image in the test set. The more detailed instructions can be found in the attached document. We will initially hire only one person for the pilot study. Once the pilot study is done, we will proceed with hiring at least 4 more people.

For further instructions, please consult the attachments. 

Desired output:
The collaboration takes two steps:
1) Technical drawing following the instructions in attachment in order to confirm (or not) that the chosen dimensions are doing well, fine-tune the design with extra attention for the constructibility (for example: does the placement of the scales on the cylinder leaves enough space to attach them) and adjustments if necesarry. Fine-tune the design.
2) Delivering files for the metal suppliers (CAD drawing of the cylinder & placement of the holes)

Please note that I do not posses specific programs to consult 3D files. Thank you in advance for delivering me files that are easy to consult (at least for the first step).

Description:

Budget is based on experience, and we are willing to pay a premium for the right talent and to retain a long term working relationship. 

Please include an example of any automotive rendering work; we are looking for 90%+ photo-realism, not cartoon or animated style.

Job Title: 3D Artist Needed to Build Interior Scenes in Blender
Description:
We are building Storyboarder, a tool that helps people tell visual stories. At its core, it feels like an easy to use 3D scene editor. We need help creating lots of interior scenes. 

Ideally, a good artist would be:

- Good knowledge and proficiency in Blender.

- Ability to model with lower polygon counts in mind. Not low-poly stylistically, but rather not super detailed where it doesn’t matter. Basically like modelling for game engines.

- Ability to model quickly. These scenes are for getting the idea of a setting, not to be ultra realistic. That said, we don’t want the objects to look bad. It’s a balance.

- Designing to correct scale. Our engine uses 1 unit = 1 meter, so it’s important that table, chair heights conform to reasonably standard dimensions.

The workflow would be:

1. Gather some photo reference for review.
2. Design, model, and texture the scenes in Blender.
3. Review and make changes.
4. Take each item out of the scene and make it its own object.
    1. Make those objects customizable by color
    2. If an object needs morph targets we can add it. (Example: Glasses of different shapes)
    3. If an object needs some basic rigging, we can add it. (Example: Box opening. Car door.)
5. Assemble the objects in the tool to create the scenes.

Examples of interior scenes: Rooms in a Home, Office, Restaurant, Bar, School, Hospital, Museum, Airport, Shop.

We’d like to try to make 1 scene and see what it’s like working together. If everything is good, we’d love to have you make lots of scenes with us!

We are looking for a Blender developer with python experience, that can help us to create an automated system for doing cloud rendering.

if there are other listings in the sheet, then it progresses to update those too.

The system must be able to handle hundreds of requests and process them accordingly.

We are looking for an experience python developer who knows how to program for Blender automation.
Candidates must have examples of previous work.

Job Title: Experienced WordPress Vue Developer Needed for Ongoing Work
Description:
Member Splash is a fast growing SaaS platform that provides membership management tools to recreational facilities across the United States. We're looking to establish long term relationships with developers, either as full or part-time hires or for ongoing contract work.

About Us: We run a Software as a Service (SaaS) platform that has doubled in size each of the last three years and now serves clients across the United States. While the back end is powered by WordPress the front end and dashboard largely use the REST API and Vue.js. We have also developed a number of custom WordPress plugins that we use internally and a few of those have been released publicly.

REQUIRED SKILLS
WordPress: You know WordPress in depth. You’ve dug into the core code and understand how it works. If you needed to modify a built-in REST response you could, or you know where to turn to figure it out. You write clean, well commented code that someone coming behind you would be able to easily follow.

Vue.js / Vuex / Vue Router: All of our interfaces are built with (or being ported to) Vue. You understand Vue.js features, patterns and best practices. Good knowledge of vanilla javascript is helpful as well.

UI Frameworks: You have solid experience with a UI framework like Bootstrap. We use Vuetify.js, a Material Design framework, so bonus if you’re already familiar with it.

APIs — We’re steadily shifting all of our code to being API based and frequently build tools that leverage third party APIs like SendGrid, Authorize.net, Google, etc.

Git — Solid understanding of a standard Git workflow: branch / pull request / merge. We don’t honestly often use Git’s more advanced commands but if you needed to revert to a prior commit you could.

Composer — our PHP code is all object oriented and namespaced and we use autoloading to handle dependencies.

Node — we use Vue-cli so you won’t often be working with Node directly but experience with it is definitely a plus.

Webpack — automates all of the development and build processes. Linting, minifying, etc. A decent understanding of how to adjust Webpack configurations would be helpful.

Grunt — we try to automate as many things as possible and a stack of handy Grunt tasks are part of that.

The skills listed above don’t cover everything you’ll need in your toolbox and we don’t expect that you’ll necessarily have all of them right now. But you should feel comfortable with a majority of them and with your ability to pick up new skills as you go.

The things listed above aren't a checklist of skills you need to already have. They're examples of what we currently use to do our work and if you start working with us you'll have the opportunity to learn and work with them as well.

What You Can Expect: If you work with us you'll get clear project specs that detail what the end goals are -- how something needs to work -- and realistic expectations for delivering it. You'll have direct communication with our in-house development team and timely responses to any questions. You'll get prompt payment and have the opportunity for bonuses based on meeting goals.

IMPORTANT: You MUST be able to provide examples of your code, not just links to sites you have worked on. We understand that prior work may be confidential and can't be provided in full but code samples from a project that demonstrate your proficiency and approach are extremely important.

Please provide links to your Github/GitLab profile or open source projects you contributed to and/or any other representative examples of your work that are relevant to the position. If you are active in communities like StackOverflow, please let us know as well

Job Title: Entrepreneurial dev wanted to build plugin, dashboard, and API integration
Description:
We're a couple of co-founders highly experienced in tech and marketing. We are looking for a developer who is passionate about building this project with us. If you're not the most experienced developer, our technical co-founder can coach and guide you through the application architecture. However, we do require some experience and most importantly the drive to gain experience in writing hot, hot code. 

    We want to team up with someone who's as excited about this project as we are. We'll pay you, but we need someone who is curious and always asking questions. You should be the type of person who doesn't stop until a problem is solved and who loves to think outside the box. To put it simply, we want you to give a fuck. We are not expecting you to solve all of our problems, but we can't do all of the googling for you. We have hit multiple walls on this project and we have always overcome them -- we need you to have that same energy. This is a truly innovative project.

    If you're reading this, you're probably an entrepreneur at heart (You're already in charge of your own business). We're all about that and want to help you feed that passion. Whether you're an experienced developer looking for a cool project to work on, or a fresh grad with fire in your belly, we want you. No need to worry about fancy credentials or titles.

There are sort of four aspects to this project:

- A Shopify plugin
- A backend for storage plus build out a RESTful API for access to the backend (you can use PaaS, cloud native services, or if you're a DevOps guru, build out your services)
- A web-based user dashboard that displays the converged data from the plugin, the backend, and 3rd-party services
- Integration with 3rd-party APIs to do relatively simple data pulls that will get stored in the backend and surfaced in the user dashboard

    You can write in any language that makes sense for that aspect of the project. Shopify will definitely require JavaScript, an understanding of JSON, and optionally PHP if you don’t want to do everything in node. The backend could likely be Go, PHP, or Python. 3rd-party integrations will require basic REST calls, but you could use some 3rd-party PHP (or there might be Python) SDKs that are out there. The data storage architecture is up to you if you choose, or we can help with that, as well, but again, cloud-native or PaaS offerings are likely fine choices here.

    We can help with visual design, data flow, API selection for 3rd-party integration, and designing the application architecture (a good bit of work has already been done here). You bring the coding chops and the burning desire to join our little team.

    The code for our project will be closed source. Though we are open source fans and encourage consuming and potentially contributing to open source projects. Eventually, open sourcing aspects of what gets built is also on the table.

    To ensure we're finding the right fit for our team and to filter out some of the auto-applications, we'd love to learn more about a project you've worked on in the past (whether for work, school, or personal) that required creative thinking and problem-solving. If you make it onto our "hot list" we'll ask for some code samples at that stage.

Looking to build an App with AppSheet that integrates with Google Sheets as a database for a small business to manager their data.

The business is a Drum Teacher who runs multiple Courses and Classes at various locations to Students.

The business owner needs to be able to use the app on their phone to easily record data that are occurring daily in their business like student registrations, student attendance, student payments, teacher payments, course and class details, general and specific course related expenses including teacher payments based on specific formulas based on attendance. The app needs to be able to generate reports based on the data added to easily show the business owner their aggregated data for profitability, reporting on business activity statements, and knowing if any student owes them money or has credits.

The app will need to do the following:

1. Add/Update/Delete Courses (name, location, start date, end date, number of classes)
2. Add/Update/Delete Classes that are child objects of the Course
3. Add/Update/Delete Teacher and Student profiles
4. Assign Teacher to each Class and report on a teachers income based on Class attendance from Students
5. Track Student transactions with a form entry that tracks, student name, description of transaction (drum class/course), amount of transaction, how they paid (cash/bank transfer/credit card)
6. Report on each students transactions, segmented and aggregated by date.
7. Add/Update/Delete attendance which is a relationship between a Class and a Student along with what pass they used to attend eg. if they used a onetime payment to attend, used a course credit to attend etc.
8. Summary of students transaction and attendance records to be able to know if a student has used up their credits or have paid for all of their attendances.
9. Add/Update/Delete Expenses with category, amount, date, who paid, who bought from (company can be added to a supplier list eventually for easy re-selection), track if it is related to a specific course or not to be able to report on profitability of a specific course.
10. Report on monthly, quarterly annual data for profit and loss overall and for each course looking at attendance records for income the data and expenses by course for expense data.
11. Report on income for teachers based on a specific formula either per class fixed rate, percentage of total income or per student fee. This formula woudl be set on the Teacher profile and used when decidinf their pay over a specific time frame.
12. To be able to add teacher pay as an expense and relate them also as a supplier in expense logging.

We would like to explore using AppSheet for this as a quick and easy way to build an app experience that integrates with data from Google Sheets.

The initial build doesn't need to be too complicated, just data entry and basic reporting.

The view should be dynamic, intuitive, easy to understand and navigate. The attached conceptual image is only that, a concept, suggestions are welcome. Ideally, the 3D image of the house should be interactive and capable of clearly showing which elements are suggested for upgrade.

Job Title: Node.js and site upgrade. Big Data download portal.
Description:
We are a boutique data-processing company (www.wherwe.com), looking to upgrade our website technology. We build data models for companies based on their own data as well as the data of their customers (sales-out/ till data). We collect data in two ways: either by plugging directly into the backend of customers, or through a data submission portal. 

We scrub and clean the data and then produce data models that a) feed dashboards and b) download portals available on our website. All users require a login, etc. 

We currently use a static (HTML) websites that embeds third part applications from two providers: Caspio and PowerBi. We currently do not rely on the API options but rather use the pre-build embed codes provided by Caspio and PowerBi. The website consists of a) login, b) submit portals, c) user editable tables that feed additional dimension data to the models and c) dasbhoards.

We want to covert our side to node.js so that we can begin to make use of the API calls. We anticipate that the API calls to Caspio will become of central importance. In addition, we want to make API calls to a SQL server on Azure (or similar). For PowerBi we anticipate that we will continue rely on the embed codes, but we are open to explore API options (though this is not central to project). 

These are the key deliverables:

-converting site to node.js (we are already hosted by a Node.js compatible server - A2 Hosting); 

- converting website code to Git with version control   (we are current not on Git), so that we can tackle modules more effectively, less messily and get up to good coding dev standards

- single sign on; currently users need to sign into our site, and then need to sign into Power BI again separately. Caspio offers SSO options that link with Azure (i.e. Microsoft authentication for PowerBi);

- creating our independent download portal - querying our own SQL database (Azure/Other)- that allows user to query and download data via CSV. Should be able to download at least 500,000 rows (max 1 million).   

- build initial API calls to Caspio and SQL Azure server, for example: 
a) create total sales per month graph, with ability to filter graph by outlet
b)  show three number in a box: total sales of last month,  growth on previous month, and growth on same month in last year
c) show three number in a box: total sales of YTD, and growth on same period last year (only for month included in YTD)
c) show a single number of total submissions on database
d) create a set of general API calls not captured above that we can then use as a start on further coding, e.g. edit table API 

This will require integration with a cool front end charting tool.

Note, at some point we may migrate fully to a SQL server, but this will not happen straight away and we will continue to rely on Caspio for some time. But we do want to select the data architecture (i.e. SQL on Azure?) which will allow us to replace Caspio in the future.

Job Title: Solve react-native IOS bug for library conflict expo-dev-client and react-native-insider
Description:
The minimum reproducible codebase is attached so you can run it directly and check the problem. Should know how expo-dev-client works

React-Native project using expo

what is expo-dev-client? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Iw8FAUftJFU&ab_channel=eveningkid

what is react-native insider? https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-native-insider

2. Running react native app on ios debug mode, with expo-dev-client, it should redirect the app to expo menu
3. Currently it only shows white screen when opening the app.
4. something in react-native-insider is blocking the expo-dev-client to go to expo menu.

libraries in conflict:
expo-dev-client
react-native-insider

How to reproduce?
download the attached zip file,
do: yarn install; cd ios; pod update; pod install; yarn run ios

when app is installed, opening it should show expo menu instead, but because of bug, it only shows white screen

deleting podspec of react-native-insider on node_modules and do: cd ios;  pod install; yarn run ios

both library modify didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:launchOptions

We're looking for the crème de la crème to help us revolutionize our customer support. Here's the plan: we're feeding 200-500 question/answer pairs into our knowledge base and then using semantic search to find the perfect answer every time a customer pops up with a query. We are seeking an experienced designer to join our team and work on updating our React web application that integrates OpenAI and Midjourney AI bots with ecommerce and NFT platforms. As a designer, you will play a critical role in helping us create an engaging and user-friendly experience for our customers.

The application will offer various prompt methodologies for the AI systems, including Single input, List input, Ask us to give you some options, and Upload photos for edit. These features will allow users to input a sentence or a few lists, and the app will create a combination of inputs and outputs that can generate a large number of images. Some ecommerce platforms, such as Etsy, require a delayed upload, and therefore our users should put their products in a queue that uploads their products at a random interval set by the user.

As a designer, you will have the opportunity to create the product forms that users will fill in to specialize their product titles, descriptions, and provide any additional information such as pricing. You will also have the chance to design the product upload process and create a visually engaging and intuitive form for users to upload their product templates.

Job Title: Update React Web App Integrating OpenAI and Midjourney AI Bots to e-commerce and NFT platforms
Description:
We are seeking an experienced developer to join our team and assist with updating our react web app. The primary goal of this project is to integrate OpenAI and Midjourney AI Bots into our existing web application. The app will provide users with a range of prompt methodologies for the AI systems, enabling them to generate unique content and upload directly to ecommerce and NFT platforms.

DETAILS -
With this update, users will have four main prompt methodologies to choose from. These methodologies include single input, list input, theme-based prompts, and photo editing. In the first methodology, users will be able to provide a sentence as input, which will generate a response from the AI system. This approach will include a list of prompts that users can choose from by clicking on them. In the second methodology, users will be able to input multiple lists, and the AI system will cycle through them, creating a combination of inputs and outputs that will generate a large number of images.

The third methodology will enable users to input a general theme, which will be used by GPT-3 to provide input options to the user. The user can then select the prompts they want to use and output. The final methodology will allow users to upload photos for editing. The AI system will use DALLE, and the user will also be able to edit the photo based on their input.

With DALLE, we will have to make API requests, and with Midjourney, we will need to manage requests to and from their Discord. It is worth noting that Midjourney does not have the "upload photos for edit" functionality.

Once the user has selected their images and chosen either ecommerce or NFT channels (or both), they will be presented with per-product forms that they can fill in to specialize their product titles, descriptions, and provide other information, such as pricing. There will also be an option to take all the data inputted, such as the prompt and the type of item the design is being sold on, and make an intriguing product title and description.

The payment process will be handled through Stripe, with options for per-image or a percentage of NFT and ecommerce sales, which must be tracked on the app and billed monthly to our users. The app will handle automatic product uploads to Opensea and Printful, with a similar approach to automation.merchtitans.com by web scraping. The printful integration will require users to upload a product template with the correct positioning, and the automated system will upload their custom AI-produced image to their store.

Finally, users will be able to directly upload the product or add the products to a section on their "drop/queue" manager. For example, NFTs are generally "dropped," where all the product uploads happen at once. Some ecommerce platforms, such as Etsy, require a delayed upload, and therefore our users should put their products in a queue that uploads their products at a random interval set by the user.

We are currently in the process of designing the application and need a developer for the next stages. The ideal candidate should have experience working with web scraping and API integrations, as well as experience with React web applications.

To apply for this position, please submit similar exemplary work, demonstrating your experience and expertise. We look forward to hearing from you and discussing this opportunity further.

Job Title: Research interesting and practical use cases for GPT-3 and other AI tools
Description:
I'd like someone to start cataloging interesting ways generative AI is transforming the way people work in different industries and professions.

The job is to go out and research articles, podcasts, and forums and then compile a list of 50 links to stories about interesting use cases for generative AI. 

To be clear, I'm not talking about broad, vague use cases like AI will be used for self-driving cars. I'm talking about very specific prompts or workflows with tools that are on the market today. The stories you link to must also include a detailed workflow or steps for people to replicate the use cases if they want to.

1. I am looking for human stories. So stories by real people who used consumer-grade AI tools to do something interesting or useful. As opposed to a faceless company anecdote.

2. I am more interested in workflows with multiple steps rather than single-use cases or examples of individual prompts. Individual prompts are OK if it's a fascinating use case, but by and large, I'm looking for examples of how people incorporated AI into their workflow to make a meaningful change in their work or life. The stories must include exact steps and prompts so that I can recreate the workflow from the post. 

Here is a blog with stories I have found so far. This should give you a sense of what I'm looking for. Please don't cover any of the stories I have already written about https://daisychainai.com/blog

To help make this clearer, I devised a simple rating system for the kinds of stories I'm looking for. The goal is to get as close to 10 points on each story as possible.

Who is the story about? (the more personal the story is the easier it is to relate to)
0 - Not sure
1 - An organization or agency, or group
2 - A person with a first and last name (the more famous the better, since it adds credibility to the story)

What was the problem they were solving with AI?
0 - AI is not solving a clear problem
1 - improving efficiency in some way
2 - solving a problem in a way non-AI alternatives just can't yet

How did they solve the problem?
0 - We don't know
1 - We have a general direction/idea of how they solved the problem
2 - We know the exact prompts/step they used

Do we know if it worked?
0 - we don't know if there was an improvement
1 - We can infer there was some improvement
2 - We have specific claims or stats around the improvement

Any considerations worth mentioning?
0 - No notes
1 point for adding best practices or gotchas worth paying attention to
1 point for plugging teh story into to a larger conversation/controversy around the issue/tool

To avoid any thoughtless, automated applications, please start your application with the sentence: I am not a robot.

Looking for an expert game designer/developer to help create two simple interactive games as part of a virtual educational course on construction project management. The games will mimic real exercises(games) that students experience as part of the in-person course.  Each game will be played by one player with 4 computer players making up the other team members. We can share video recording of the actual games, but here's a simplified description of each. 

1. Dice Game - In the dice game, players roll two 9-sided dice and pass a number of chips to the next teammate in line based on the total of their roll. The goal of the game is to move the entire pile of chips from the first teammate in line to the last. 

2. The Airplane Game - Each of the 5 players are given a specific set of lego pieces. Each player's pieces are one of 5 parts of a lego airplane. The goal of the game is for the team to build as many airplanes as possible within the given timeframe. The first time the game is played every team member gets a random set of pieces and no directions, obviously they struggle making airplanes. The second time the game is played each team member is given a group of all the same pieces (one gets all wheels, the other gets all wings, etc.) and specific directions, and an order to sit in. With this new structure the team builds a bunch of planes quickly and efficiently. 

Each game will need to be planned out from start to finish, with a clear roadmap dictating phases, key milestones, input required, etc. 

Budget is flexible, we know this isn't the most difficult game design, but we do want to do excellent work first and foremost.

*Admin can create, edit, delete Coordinator, Manager, Subscriber users
*Coordinator can create, edit, Manager, Subscriber users, but only the ones assigned to him (child's)
*Manager can create, edit, Subscriber users, but only the ones assigned to him (child's)

The Admin can make part of the text of the post in HOLD, so the user can't delete or modify that HOLD part, so needs to be part of the shared post of the User.

Admin can activate the Notification when creating a Post, if activated, it will be send immediately a Push Notification to the selected users/groups inviting to share the content to their own social networks with a few clicks.

Each post will have in each network will have a defined by Admin a Points Value, for example:
Admin creates Post "ABC" when creating he will define a value in each network, example:
Twitter = 1 point
Facebook = 2 points
Instagram = 3 points
TikTok = 2 points

So, when a user successfully shares a the post "ABC" in one or more of these networks, we will sum the points of each network to his own Balance Points, only if he really shared it. 

   B) Create group of users, with filter based search he can select in bulk users to add to Custom Groups where the admins will give a Name to the Group and assign users and ability to remove users from groups with filters as well or delete Groups.

   C) The admin can schedule any post he have created to be shown in the other user levels Advocacy Section to a total users or Group users only in a schedule Example: from 15:00 January 30 of 2023 to 15:00 January 31 2023. He can select Auto-Notification too, if he selected Auto-Notification then when the post it's available (based on the schedule) a Notification to these users will be sent when the schedule starts.

    D) The admin can send push notifications to Android and iOS apps, to specific user/groups selected, pushing with a custom text/image/video and/or link or deep link to a Post (of our system) who wants to share with the users.

    E) The admin can edit, delete, duplicate any post he made.

    F) Know, edit, delete, the points earned by each user (explained more after) 

   G) Have a metrics dashboard where he can see the total shared posts by day, week, month, year, filter by Social Network, Group, User(s).

4.-  The Users can do this:

    A)  Click to Share the Posts that the Admins user sent to them, with one or two clicks, needs to be easy and fast to share the content shared by the Admin to their personal Social Networks, they can choose the network where they want to share it, if the social network selected by User is not already with OAuth the app will request the permission to do it. 

The Post text can be edited by the User if the Admin gave that permission on that shared post, if not, the shared post needs to be exactly as the Admin created.

   B) Earn points by each real shared content (each unique post to each unique social network)

   C) Know the points they have earned until today, and see the Posts they have effective shared in their networks

The system needs to work using high security O-Auth for social network access.

The discussion app unique since one person will sign up as a Creator and create a discussion page based on a topic and then they will invite at least 2 friends to participate as Contributors. So only the Contributors can post in the discussion. 

Here are the links to the 2 flowcharts and the slack channel with the designs/
https://tinyurl.com/na6mw5vr
https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVPnKvQf4=/?share_link_id=601339458559
https://tinyurl.com/2ffpms9j

There will be KEY unique differences. 

We will have a Partner Program, similar to YouTube where 70% of our advertising revenue from each discussion page will be given to the Creator and Contributors of that discussion page. 

We will also have very vital pop up windows with important messages. In order to keep existing users signing up at least 2 more users. Each contributor will be required to sign up as a creator of another discussion page within 24 hours after signing up as a contributor to a previous discussion page. And then refer at least 2 more contributors within another 24 hours. 

So we will have pop up windows reminding them to do this. We won't implement these rules functionally but just as pop up windows. So let's say User A (creator) signs up and then they sign up the required minimum of 2 (or more) contributors to their discussion page (User B and User C). 

So User B and C will have to become creators for at least one of their own discussion pages and sign up at least 2 contributors each. One other rule is that in each discussion page, the creator and each contributor simply has to continue the discussion by adding a short (at least) 200 character response once per day. So let's say User B creates their own discussion page and then signs up 2 contributors, User D and E. 

If User B hadn't created a discussion page and signed up two contributors, they would always see a pop that reads something along the lines of "You're not adhering to the rules of the Partner Program and you may soon not be able to permanently post in any discussion page where you're either a creator or contributor".

User A will also see a message in this case that reads something like "(actual name of User B, is not adhering to the rules of the Partner Program and has not created their own discussion page. Please contact them to let them know so your discussion page may continue being a part of the partner program". 

Same thing happens with User D and E, etc. User A won't know if User D or E hasn't posted, but User B will see the same pop up if User D or E aren't following the rules.

Again, functionally, we won't actually implement this but we will lay this out as rules of the partner program and show pop up messages in these following certain situations

AND WE WILL HAVE THESE ADDITIONAL IMPORTANT FUNCTIONALITIES.

Leaderboard that will simply show the order of how many times each discussion page was simply opened in each category and then a main leaderboard that will combine all of the leaderboards together. So each category will have it's own leaderboard and then the main leaderboard.

Suggestions based on which category or subcategory your discussion page is in. As well as push notifications and email reminders with the same message as those pop up windows in-app.

Auto referral codes. So I will start with sending initial emails to a list of people and we will need to add that referral code in the system. Since I think initially it should only be invite only and the referral code expires after 48 hours. So each time a creator goes to invite a contributor and the contributor receives the email, the email will include a unique invite code that they sign up page needs to recognize.

Can we also require the users sign up with real phone numbers. So we will send them a verification text when they sign up and maybe also the first several times that they post an entry into the discussion page. So for the entry to post, they'll get a text and would need to verify it. So burner numbers or google voice numbers won't be allowed. Only actual phone numbers from actual carriers. Because I think we need to ensure that people are inviting real people so the marketing continues of real people signing up. So this way once a phone number has been used and is linked to a user, it can no longer be used by another user.

Description:
We are looking to outsource some of our development work which involves replicating our clients' site branding using our custom design tool. The tool allows developers to use HTML, CSS and Javascript to replicate the branding on our client's site. 

We are looking for someone who would like to work with us on an ongoing basis, so that we can regularly send work their way as we have requests come in. 

We provide the URL to the site for which the branding needs to be replicated, and a login for the developer to go in and use our tool to replicate the branding using HTML, CSS and Javascript. 

We need the header and footer to look and work the same as their existing site, as well as menus/navigation etc. Some bits of their header which we cannot replicate are sometimes omitted (eg a search bar which is too difficult to replicate. These things would be agreed at the beginning of starting to replicate the branding)

Sometimes we would need brandings to be created from scratch, and other times we would just need changes to be made to existing brandings. 

Attached you can see a screenshot of the design tool which is used to edit the HTML, CSS and Javascript of the design. We would also give you access to JIRA so that you can update the ticket with progress etc.

The number of hours we require are difficult to predict - there will be some weeks where we require a lot of hours, and others will not require so many.

The process will be something like this:
- We send you an email to let you know what needs doing, along with the JIRA ticket number. It may not be me who contacts you, but someone else from Passle
- When you are ready to start, you log into JIRA and move the ticket to "In progress"
- While you are in the process of completing the branding, if you find there is anything than cannot be replicated (eg if they have a search function or something which you are not able to copy) then please add details in a comment on the jira, and let the person who requested the branding know (by email)
- When you have completed the branding, you move the JIRA ticket to "Preview ready" 
- At this point, our testing team will test the branding, and if it is fine they will move the JIRA ticket to "Ready for live". If they find any issues, they will move it to "Error" and add notes to the ticket explaing any issues
- If it goes to "Error" you fix any thing that they have found and move back to "Preview ready" 
- Once the testing team move the ticket to "Ready for live", then the branding can be made live.

Job Title: Blockchain developer with Python, Ethereum network
Description:
I am looking for a blockchain developer or firm that has deep knowledge about Ethereum and Python programming to help transforming the automotive industry.
The right candidate should have deep understanding of blockchain technology and have experience building decentralized systems that can securely store and track transactions. 
Core concept:
Developing a blockchain-based transaction system for vehicles in a dealership involves several steps, including:
Deliverables:
- Define the use case: The first step is to define the problem you're trying to solve. What information do you need to track and why? How do you want to use the blockchain to improve the current process?
- Choose a blockchain platform: Based on your use case, you need to choose a suitable blockchain platform that meets your requirements. Some popular blockchain platforms for this use case include Ethereum, Hyperledger, and EOS.
- Design the blockchain network: The next step is to design the blockchain network, including the structure of the blocks, the consensus mechanism, and the smart contract logic.
- Implement the smart contracts: The smart contracts define the rules and logic of the transactions in the blockchain. You will need to write the code for the smart contracts and deploy them on the blockchain network.
- Store the vehicle data: You need to store the information about each vehicle, such as its make, model, year, VIN number, and ownership history, in the blockchain. This information can be stored in a structured database or in a more flexible NoSQL database, depending on your needs.
- Integrate with existing systems: You will need to integrate the blockchain transaction system with the existing systems in the dealership, such as the inventory management system, the accounting system, and any other relevant systems.
- Test and deploy: Finally, you need to test the blockchain transaction system thoroughly to make sure it is working as intended and meets your requirements. Once the testing is complete, you can deploy the system in the dealership.

It's important to note that developing a blockchain transaction system is a complex process that requires specialised knowledge and skills. 

Responsibilities:
- Design the data structure: Determine the data structure for the blocks that will be added to the blockchain. Each block should contain information about a vehicle transaction, such as the vehicle's make, model, year, VIN number, and transaction date. You may also want to include information about the buyer and seller, such as their names and addresses.
- Implement the blockchain: Write the code for the blockchain in a programming language such as Python, JavaScript, or Go. You can use a framework such as Hyperledger Fabric, Ethereum, or a blockchain platform such as IBM Blockchain Platform to simplify the implementation process.
- Test the blockchain: Thoroughly test the blockchain to ensure that it is functioning correctly and is secure against potential attacks. You may want to consider hiring a security firm to perform a penetration test to identify any vulnerabilities in the system.

Description:
Hi!

We are looking for an experienced software/coding advisor (familiar with existing video conferencing software currently available on the market, website coding tools and mobile applications) to facilitate and create the architecture for our project. 

We are a Christian organization. Our goal is to create a website and a mobile phone app that will allow users (who are directed by various types of advertising) to give their life to Jesus Christ. Upon seeing a billboard or digital advertising a user will be directed to a specific "website" or mobile application. This application will have strong video conferencing capabilities.

Here are the steps:

1. User logs in to the website or mobile application.

2. User is welcomed with a set of questions that will determine user's profile.

7. The website and mobile application will also need to facilitate multiple users and counselors to communicate at the same time and also multiple users and counselors to communicate individually in separate "rooms".

8. There will need to be functionality that manages the "waiting room" and/or bottleneck system. That is, if there are multiple users logging in at the same time and there are not enough counselors those users will be kept in the waiting room until available counselors have been notified and opted-in. Additionally, there will need to functionality that allows for one counselor to speak with multiple users and multiple counselors to speak with multiple users simultaneously.

Please apply ONLY if you are an experienced software architect and able to start working on this project immediately.

Thank you!

Job Title: UX/UI design project funding application portal
Description:
We are seeking a UX/UI designer to create wireframes, visual designs, and UX and flow for a funding portal. The designer should aim to create an intuitive and user-friendly experience for potential grantees.

The project will involve creating wireframes and prototypes to test and refine the design of the portal. The designer should conduct user research to understand the needs and goals of potential grantees, and use this information to inform the design of the portal. The wireframes and prototypes should be used to solicit feedback from potential grantees and to iterate on the design as needed.

The designer should also create a visual design for the portal that is consistent with the branding and values of the organization. This includes designing a color scheme, typography, and other visual elements that create a cohesive and visually appealing experience.

In addition, the designer should create an information architecture that is easy to navigate and understand. This includes designing a clear and consistent navigation system, as well as organizing content in a logical and intuitive manner.

Overall, the UX/UI designer is responsible for creating a user-centered design that meets the needs of potential grantees and helps them navigate the grant application process with ease. The designer should work closely with the development team to ensure that the design is implemented effectively and efficiently.

The project:

The funding portal will be designed with a variety of features to streamline the grant application process and enable effective communication between the organization and potential grantees.

One key feature will be a login system that allows applicants to create a secure account and access the various forms and resources available on the portal.

Another critical feature will be the various forms available to potential grantees. These will include a pre-application form, which will allow applicants to provide basic information about their project and receive feedback before submitting a full application. The full application form will be comprehensive, enabling applicants to provide detailed information about their project, budget, timeline, expected outcomes, and more. In addition, there will be an application form specifically for donations, allowing individuals and organizations to make contributions directly to supported projects. Finally, the portal will feature a transfer application form, enabling current grantees to request additional funding or make adjustments to their grant.

The funding portal will also feature robust file management capabilities. Applicants will be able to upload all necessary documents and materials through the portal, ensuring that the organization has all the information it needs to make informed decisions about grant applications. The portal will also allow for easy tracking and management of all grant-related documents, such as project proposals, budgets, and reporting materials.

Overall, the funding portal will be an essential tool for ensuring effective communication and efficient grant management. By providing a streamlined process for submitting grant applications, managing files, and communicating with potential grantees, the portal will help the organization achieve its mission of making a positive impact in the community.

Job Title: Real-time Web-Page Updates using WebSockets, PHP, Javascript
Description:
I am seeking a highly skilled developer who possesses experience in SQL triggers, websockets, JavaScript, and PHP. The goal of this project is to implement a real-time notification system on our website.

The ideal candidate will be an experienced developer who can implement real-time data updates in an HTML table using WebSockets. The system should be built using PHP for the server-side code, Ratchet (or similar) for WebSocket implementation, and JavaScript for the client-side code.

The system should function as follows:

Firstly, set up a WebSocket server using the Ratchet PHP library or a similar library to handle incoming connections from clients.

Next, a trigger will be created in the MySQL database table "records" that will fire every time a new row is inserted into the table. The trigger should verify if the inserted row satisfies certain conditions (e.g., if the "foo" column equals "bar"). If the condition is satisfied, the trigger should send the relevant data to a websocket server.

The websocket server should broadcast the data to all connected users who meet specific criteria (e.g., if the user has the necessary permissions to see the data). Websocket authentication and authorization mechanisms should be used to achieve this.

On the client side, use JavaScript to listen for WebSocket messages. Whenever a new message is received, use JavaScript to fetch the new row from the server via AJAX and add it to the HTML table without refreshing the page.

Finally, the websocket server should have a mechanism for enabling/disabling the trigger based on the presence of connected users. Disable the MySQL trigger if no clients are connected, and enable it again when at least one client is connected.

The ideal candidate should possess experience in:

PHP and SQL triggers
Websocket implementation using Ratchet or a similar library
Websocket authentication and authorization mechanisms
Working with large datasets and optimizing database performance
The candidate should be proficient in building dynamic web applications and have a solid understanding of JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. Additionally, the candidate should have excellent communication skills.

Job Title: Web3 development: make existing React website interactive with smart contract
Description:
We are looking for a front end web3 developer who can do the required wiring to connect a react.js website to an associated smart contract, which we will redeploy. We currently have a website moddelled after (link removed)/ (all tabs), but it has no web3 functionality and currently uses dummy data (i.e., no real dataflow implemented). The deliverable will be code that makes our current website interactive with the already deployed NFTX contracts (https://docs.nftx.io/smart-contracts/contract-addresses).

The nftx.io site calls NFTX-owned centralised APIs, which may require authorization to ping, so for this project, just the raw contract interactions can be wired in first. However, some features, such as searching for NFTs to buy, might be powered by these APIs, so eventually, we might need to recreate these apis with either our own centralised server or (preferably) a subgraph, if the contract events are sufficient.

User inputs written to the blockchain should appropriately open MetaMask modals. There also needs to be a data flow in from the blockchain that regularly updates both user-specific and non-user-specific data at settable intervals. These should then be distributed to the various pages using state management (e.g., Redux) with minimal lead redundancy across different query needs.

Please use the ABI from etherscan and the ethers.js library for wiring. The npm web3Modal or WalletConnect libraries should be used for the site's wallet connection. the ethers.BigNumber library must be used for numeric value handling of token/wei values. The ethers.utils libraries should be used to format the numeric values to human-readable strings. In the rare instance where fractional mathematics are required, the npm bignumber.js package can be used.

The candidate should be familiar with blockchain development testing procedures. For example, It will be helpful to run the contracts on a local node. There are a variety of possible solutions you could use, but we use the hardhat local node feature internally.

Job Title: Build API integrations to multiple AI apps including StableDiffusion, text to voice, and video
Description:
About Us

Kid Creative is a developmental stage company backed by founders who have successfully formed, built and exited multiple companies. Kid Creative’s initial product will be a video that tells a children’s story where the child watching the video is the story’s main character. We will capture the requisite information about the child (name, age, birthdate, etc. as well as pics) via a web front end; transmit the data via API feeds to a range of different AI vendors (image generators such as WallE or Stable Diffusion; voice generators like Revoicer; et al) and then take the returned files and have a custom video auto built and transmitted to the purchaser of the video (typically the child’s parent). This will be the initial service, and significant product expansion is planned after its release.

We are Seeking:

We are looking for an experienced outside contractor to lead the development of an automated process to create the personalized videos. The successful candidate will be responsible for creating a front-end UI to capture the requisite data as well as integrating with multiple third-party APIs to transmit and receive data and files. This project will involve several steps, including error handling and sequencing rules. Experience with video creation a strong plus and api feeds of the types of companies referenced above is a strong plus.
A candidate located in the Los Angeles or Portland area is a plus but not required.

Responsibilities:

•	Design and develop a front-end UI to capture user data and file components, including defining rules around the gathering of such elements.
•	Create a series of API integrations with a variety of third-party applications, and ensure that data and files are transmitted correctly according to defined rules and sequencing.
•	Develop an error handling process for when data and files are not received or transmitted correctly.
•	Receive data and files back from the APIs and store them as necessary.
•	Transmit returned elements to additional APIs to create a finished product.
Requirements:
•	Extensive experience with API integrations, preferably in a similar project.
•	Proven track record in developing and implementing successful automated processes.
•	Ability to design and develop front-end UIs to capture data and files in a user-friendly way.
•	Strong problem-solving skills, with a focus on error handling and sequencing rules.
•	Excellent communication skills to collaborate with a remote team and communicate with stakeholders.
•	Ability to work independently.

The project will be completed in 5 phases with each phase having a set of agreed upon deliverables. The first phase will be a proof of concept without a web application and is intended to prove API support for all requisite data elements to generate the personalized video. 

If you have the required experience and expertise, and are passionate about developing an innovative automated process to create personalized videos, we invite you to submit your application.

Job Title: Physical asset counting mobile app using React Native
Description:
The desired project is an Android application that is compatible with Zebra Android devices, specifically those equipped with a Zebra RFID reader gun. The application will utilize a REST API to obtain a list of locations and assets. The user will initiate a "count session" within the app, where they will read the location using an RFID or barcode tag. All devices located in that specific location will then be listed, and the user will use the RFID reader feature of the device and app to count the assets. As the user counts each device, the app will update the device list to indicate that the device has been counted.

The application should function offline while the user is counting. Once the device is back online, the count results should be sent to the REST API server. The app should also have access to all previous count sessions and results through the REST API server to prevent duplicate counting.

The app's user interface should be developed using the React Native framework, and the code language should be Typescript. The application can utilize any offline database system. If any additional clarification is required, please let me know.

Job Title: Developer needed for updating to the latest Facebook SDK for iOS.
Description:
I am looking for someone to implement the below required updates, it's a 1-time project.

Step 1: Update the Facebook SDK for iOS

Using Cocoapods
If your app integrates with the Facebook SDK for iOS using Cocoapods follow these steps.

1. Add the code to the podfile for the packages that are used in your app.

Example:

pod 'FBSDKCoreKit' '~ 8.0.0'
pod 'FBSDKLoginKit' '~ 8.0.0'
pod 'FBSDKShareKit' '~ 8.0.0'
pod 'FBSDKGamingServiceKit' '~ 8.0.0'
2. Run pod update.


Using Swift Package Manager (SPM)
If your app uses SPM to integrate with the Facebook SDK for iOS follow these steps.

1. In Xcode click File  Swift Packages  Add Package Dependency.

2. In Package Repository enter the repository URL: https://github.com/facebook/facebook-ios-sdk.

3. In Version select Up to Next Major and the default option.

4. Complete the prompts to select the libraries you want to use in your project.

Recommended:

Turn on Advertiser Tracking Enabled
AdvertiserTrackingEnabled is a setting that allows you to receive a status from iOS 14 devices. When set to Yes or True, you can monitor the number of devices that are sending certain data within the app. Without AdvertiserTrackingEnabled turned on app events from iOS 14 devices will not be counted, which will impact ad campaign performance. By default AdvertiserTrackingEnabled is set to No or False.

The Advertiser Tracking Enabled topic in the Facebook Developer documentation shows you how to enable and disable advertising tracking.

The purpose of this project is to develop an app called "Neighbourhood Kitchen", a platform that enables students who cook for themselves to sell their extra or leftover food to others in their neighbourhood. The app is designed to solve the issue of food insecurity among students and reduce food waste. The platform should have a user-friendly interface, be easy to navigate, and have essential features such as location tracking, photo capturing, and order management.



Instructions:



User Registration:
The app should have a sign-up/log-in process for users to create an account.
Users should be able to provide their basic information, such as name, email address, and phone number.
The app should also allow users to set their location so that they can be matched with other users in their neighbourhood.
Posting Food Items:
Users should be able to post what they are cooking on a particular day, including the type of food, the serving size, and the price.
The app should have a photo-capturing feature that allows users to upload a picture of their food.
Users should also be able to specify the number of extra servings they are willing to make.
Order Management:
Users should be able to view a list of food items posted by others in their neighbourhood.
They should be able to place an order by clicking on a food item and specifying the number of servings they would like to purchase.
The app should have a feature that allows users to track their orders and see the status of each order.
Location Tracking:
The app should have a location tracking feature that allows users to view a map of the food items available in their neighbourhood.
Users should be able to search for food items based on their location, distance, and food type.
Cleanliness Rating:
Users should be able to rate the cleanliness of the cooking environment for each food item posted.
This feature will help to increase consumer confidence and ensure food safety.
Payment and Delivery:
The app should have a payment gateway that allows users to make payments securely.
Users should be able to arrange for delivery or pick-up of the food items they have purchased.
User Feedback:
The app should have a feedback feature that allows users to provide feedback on the food items they have purchased.
This feature will help to improve the overall quality of the food offered on the platform.
Admin Panel:
The app should have an admin panel that allows administrators to monitor and manage the platform.
The admin panel should have features such as user management, food item management, and order management.
Conclusion:



Neighbourhood Kitchen is a unique and innovative app that provides a solution to food insecurity and food waste among students. The app should have a user-friendly interface, essential features such as location tracking and photo capturing, and a cleanliness rating system to ensure food safety. The app should also have a payment gateway and an admin panel to monitor and manage the platform.

TAGS - I have a masterlist of tags for each hero.

Job Title: WordPress Technical Manager for Cloud-Native Sites
Description:
We seek a WordPress Technical Manager to join our team and help build, maintain, and support cloud-native WordPress sites. You’ll be working with the latest web technologies to design fast and secure solutions.

The ideal candidate is an experienced software engineer who loves solving complex problems and, has experience managing websites on AWS, GCP, or Azure cloud platforms, and is interested in learning more about the cloud.

- Create and maintain WordPress websites in development, staging, and production environments
- Customize themes in and extend GravityForms, Metabox, SiteOrigin, etc. functionality in a modular way
- Collaborate with other team members in branches, Pull Requests, and on Slack
- Understand the business model, customer journey, and KPIs

## Project Stack

- WordPress: We use WordPress as our standard CMS for all our content-rich sites. Our DevSecOps platform provides us with full automation for development, testing, staging, and production environments.
- GravityForms: We use GravityForms for booking events, such as setting up tournament registration, payment processing, and other forms that need to be completed for the event.
- MetaBox: Used to create custom fields in our WordPress websites
- SiteOrigin: Used to build custom pages with drag & drop functionality
- Tailwind CSS: Our CSS framework of choice used to style our websites
- Stripe API: We use Stripe's API to provide payment processing on the website.
- HubSpot API: We use HubSpot for sales and customer support, including website analytics.
- Jira: Used to track and manage tasks and stories
- Confluence: Used as a collaboration tool where teams can document processes and create standards
- Slack: Helps teams communicate quickly while empowered with ChatOps.
- GitHub: Version control system for tracking changes made over time and feature-driven development
- NewRelic: Used to monitor website performance, and our alerts are source-controlled.
- Kubernetes: Used to manage our containers for deployment.
- Docker: Used to create and run containers for our development, staging, and production environments.
- CloudFront: Content delivery network used to accelerate content loading on the website.

## Principles
- Remote Development: We use remote development to ensure our team members have access to the latest website version and can work from anywhere.
- Continuous Delivery: We use continuous delivery to ensure that we deploy changes quickly, efficiently, and securely.
- Security First: We take security seriously at all times and make sure our servers are safe from vulnerabilities and cyber threats

## Interview and Onboarding Process
The interview and onboarding process for this position is as follows:

- Selection (if you see this,  you've made it!)
- Screening Questions (5 of them, nothing hard)
- Interview in Chat (discussing your experiences and skills)
- Dev Evaluation (we give you a story to complete and commit)
- Working Evaluation (we ask you to work on a project for two weeks)
- Technical Manager Training (you will be trained in our platform and technologies)

We look forward to hearing from you!

1.	User registration and login: The app should allow users to create their profiles and log in using their credentials or social media accounts.

7.	User feedback and support: The app should have a feature to enable users to provide feedback on the app's functionality and to report any issues or problems they encounter.
8.	Admin Panel: An Admin panel should be provided to manage and maintain the app, including tool listings, tool owners, user information, and app content.
Non-functional Requirements:
1.	Security: The app should ensure the security of user data and payment transactions.
2.	Performance: The app should be responsive and fast to ensure a smooth user experience.
3.	Scalability: The app should be scalable to handle the growth of the user base and data.
4.	Availability: The app should be available 24/7 to ensure that users can access the tool rental services at any time.
5.	Compatibility: The app should be compatible with both iOS and Android platforms.
Conclusion: The above requirements outline the core functionalities and features of the tool-sharing app. With the right design, development, and implementation, the app has the potential to become a reliable platform for renting and sharing tools, making it easier and more affordable for users to get the tools they need for their projects.

Job Title: Learn & Be paid - .NET microservices app with React and GraphQL

Hello developers from a developer :)

The scope of this project is to build an application which will be presented to some students in an educational purpose, so it’s not planned to be shipped to customers. Therefore, I’d like to present as many technologies and design patterns and not to spend time on a perfect security, GDPR, landing pages, SEO, etc. It’s a good oportunity for you to learn and test new technologies that you didn’t have time before (and be paid for it).

A basic implementation will contain: user authentification / registration, adding new house for sale (as many information as possible - name, description, photos, location, additional information, etc.), listing and filtering for on-sale houses, live bidding (using graphql subscriptions), notifications, etc. The user stories are defined based on the technical implementations.

Due to the flexible requirements, based on your experience and your learning willingness, you can choose what additional features you’d like to implement (for example, mesh services, metrics, load balancer, push notifications, loggings, tracing, etc.). The front-end design must be easy to use, but not something complicated. The only requirement is to be responsive (using an existing template is fine), so you can utilize a React component library (for instance, Material UI).
-	Any other high-end technologies that you are passionate. For instance, using blockchain to store in a secure way the owner of the house, different types of databases for different services (SQL or no-SQL), payment implementation with Stripe (testing account only), 3D model presentation for the houses, Azure OpenAI, etc. (sky is the limit).

Therefore, if you’d like to use new technologies, unleash you imagination, come up with proactive ideas and learn through practicing, I want to work with you. Let’s learn together.

Goal: Convert existing Python/Django interface to our required PHP framework we have created that acts as the Front End to our Asterisk PBX.
